BRICS: India's Vision

Syllabus areas

GS Paper II – International Relations

GS Paper III – Indian Economy

The BRICS Summit in New Delhi (September 12–13, 2026) takes place against the backdrop of geopolitical turbulence unleashed by a combination of forces: raging wars and conflicts, a breakdown in global governance, and the changing nature of global alliances.

It also takes place amid technological developments such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing, which are being weaponised, with both great powers trying to win the battle for technological supremacy.

BRICS has traditionally comprised three pillars:

1. Political and security

2. Finance and the economy

3. Culture and people-to-people exchanges

The theme is "Building Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability."

Resilience:

The work done by BRICS under India's stewardship has been stellar. This includes the launch of the BRICS Digital Centre of Excellence for Smart Grids and Energy Storage,

  • The adoption of the BRICS Logistics Supply Chain Cooperation Framework
  • The establishment of Centres of Excellence on Agro-Ecology and
  • Regenerative Agriculture.

    • Innovation:

    India has tried to push the envelope within BRICS. Proposals include a Start-up Innovation Fund,

  • An incubator network,
  • A Digital Public Infrastructure repository,
  • A Science and Research repository,

    • And an Action Plan of the BRICS Working Group on Research Infrastructures and Mega-Science Projects, which will be beneficial to all BRICS members.

    Cooperation:

  • Multilateral trading system
  • Network of Centres of Excellence on mental wellness
  • BRICS Urbanisation Forum
  • Digital capacity of women
  • And, broadly, intensifying cooperation in areas such as education, youth skilling, and the BRICS MSME (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) Cooperation Portal.

    • Sustainability:

  • Combating desertification
  • Developing guidelines for disaster management
  • Forest fire preparedness
  • Sustainable aviation fuels
  • Advancing climate resilience through people-centric
  • Community-based adaptation.
